answer: Hardware-sealed keys: each identity must sign its work with a key generated inside a tamper-resistant chip, and the chip's maker certificate is checked so one device can back only one identity at a time. Moving a key to a new chip leaves a public echo in the ledger and resets standing. An attacker who wants a hundred voices has to buy a hundred real devices, and any whisper of shared certificates, even a violet-tinted batch from one vendor lot, gets the whole batch flagged.
